dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.text: What did you think of the exhibition? You seemed to enjoy it.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Very much. The curator chose the pieces very carefully.

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.text: I agree. Which work impressed you most?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: The large painting in the last room. It is considered a masterpiece.

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.text: Why do you think it is so famous?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Perhaps because it shows ordinary people in a very honest way.

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.text: Interesting. I listened to the audio guide, and it gave a very different explanation.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Art is open to interpretation, which is what makes museums exciting.

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.text: True. Some people say museums should not be so expensive.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I think entry should be cheap, because culture belongs to everyone.

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.text: But maintaining cultural heritage costs a lot of money.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That is a valid point. Perhaps free days each month could be a compromise.

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.text: Many cities already do that, and the museums become very crowded.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Crowds are a good sign, though: they show that people value art.

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.text: Fair enough. Shall we visit the modern art museum next weekend?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Gladly. This time I will download the audio guide in advance.
